subject: ent
title: Chronic otitis media and cholesteatoma

steps.tx: **Chronic otitis media** means persistent middle ear and mastoid inflammation with drum perforation and discharge lasting weeks. Safe (tubotympanic) disease has a central perforation with mucosal infection and conductive loss but low complication risk. Unsafe (atticoantral) disease has attic or marginal perforation harbouring cholesteatoma that erodes bone toward brain, labyrinth and facial nerve.
steps.say: Chronic ear disease is perforation plus lasting discharge. Central holes are safer; attic disease with cholesteatoma erodes toward brain and balance organs.

steps.tx: **Cholesteatoma** is keratinising squamous epithelium growing into the middle ear and mastoid, trapping desquamated keratin that expands, infects (often Pseudomonas and anaerobes) and erodes ossicles, labyrinth and tegmen. Acquired disease follows retraction pockets from Eustachian dysfunction sucking the drum attic inward, or migration through marginal perforations. Congenital cholesteatoma grows behind an intact drum in children.
steps.say: Cholesteatoma is skin growing in the wrong place, trapping keratin and eroding bone. Retraction pockets from poor ventilation create most acquired cases.

vis.alt: Diagram showing acquired cholesteatoma formation. A retraction pocket in the tympanic membrane's attic invaginates, accumulating keratin debris that expands and erodes ossicles.
vis.caption: Cholesteatoma: acquired formation via retraction pocket or migration. Image: welleschik, CC BY 2.5, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: **Key point.** Patients report painless foul discharge unresponsive to drops, conductive deafness and sometimes vertigo, facial weakness or headache warning of complications. Otoscopy shows attic crust or white keratin mass. CT temporal bone maps erosion; diffusion MRI detects residual pearls after surgery. Audiometry grades conductive versus sensorineural loss.
steps.say: Foul painless discharge ignoring drops plus attic white mass means cholesteatoma. Scans map erosion before surgery.

steps.tx: Treatment is surgical: **mastoidectomy** removes disease and creates a safe dry ear, with tympanoplasty reconstructing drum and ossicles when possible. Canal wall up preserves anatomy but risks hidden recurrence needing second look; canal wall down exteriorises disease for surveillance at cost of a mastoid cavity needing lifelong care. Medical therapy only temporises.
steps.say: Only surgery removes cholesteatoma. Wall up hides recurrence; wall down needs cavity care. Drops alone never cure it.

right.title: Unsafe CSOM
points: Bone erosion, brain and labyrinth risk

steps.tx: **Key point.** Safe central perforations are kept dry (water precautions), treated with toilet and topical therapy for discharge, then offered myringoplasty once dry, improving hearing and infection resistance. Children with bilateral disease and deafness get hearing support meanwhile. Any chronic ear with vertigo, palsy or fever becomes urgent.
steps.say: Keep safe perforations dry, clean infected flares, close dry holes surgically. Vertigo or facial weakness with chronic ear is urgent.
